title: Vietnam Solar Plant Performance Monitor
thesis: Snowflake turns daily inverter data from a fictional solar operator's Vietnam plants (ground-mount fixed-tilt, single-axis tracker, floating, rooftop C&I and solar-plus-storage) into in-range performance KPIs, 7-day generation loss risk scores, inverter temperature anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: In-range inverter readings, generation loss events, faults per 1,000 string checks and inverter readings for 30 solar plants across 6 Vietnam cities.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it traces back to plant-day rows and the inverter readings behind them.
The out-of-range chart shows which loss causes push the most inverter readings below the expected performance-ratio band.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of plant performance KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which plants are likely to have the next generation loss event?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each plant's probability of a generation loss event in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags peak inverter temperature outliers per plant, and the forecast projects fleet-wide inverter-reading volume for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: How ready are the spare parts behind those risks?

talking_points: Plant availability and spare-parts readiness (string inverters, tracker drive motors, pontoon float kits, inverter cooling fans and battery modules) frame the response capacity.
Module-cleaning PM compliance against in-range inverter readings by plant shows where maintenance discipline and performance move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, generation loss event, cause and risk tables only.
show: PM compliance vs in-range inverter readings
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when an inverter raises a temperature alarm right now?

talking_points: Live inverter readings (peak heatsink temperature in C, inverter load) land in RAW.LIVE_TELEMETRY, from the Snowflake simulator or from AWS IoT Core through S3 and Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs ALARM readings with an SOP hint and the plant's current risk band, then emails the O&M technician.
tabs.call_out: From alarm to action in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over synthetic generation loss response SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (IoT Core, S3, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
